claims: Ford is recalling nearly 1.4 million 2015–2017 F-150 trucks in the U.S.
The recall is due to a software issue that may cause unexpected downshifts to second gear
Unexpected downshifts to second gear potentially result in loss of control
The recall affects vehicles with 6R80 transmissions
Repairs involve a powertrain control module (PCM) software update
Approximately 1.39 million 2015-2017 Ford F-150 pickups equipped with 6-speed automatic transmissions are affected
A signal loss between the transmission range sensor and the powertrain control module can cause an abrupt downshift to second gear
The issue can cause rear wheels to lock up
Rear wheels locking up increases the risk of a crash
Ford is aware of two injuries related to this issue
Ford is aware of one accident related to this issue
Dealers will update the powertrain control module software for free
Over 103,000 2023-2025 F-150s with trailer tow packages were recalled due to potential broken rear axle hub bolts
Potential broken rear axle hub bolts can cause power loss
Potential broken rear axle hub bolts can cause rollaway
Nearly 12,000 2023-2024 F-150 Lightning EVs were recalled for a potential steering control arm detachment
A separate 2026 recall affects various models including 2021-2026 F-150s
The 2026 recall involves a software update to prevent potential loss of trailer brakes
